title: NURBS surfaces with exact sphere and torus
purpose: Evaluate and tessellate tensor-product NURBS surfaces, including exact spheres and tori built as surfaces of revolution from rational profiles. Use it for CAD-style surfaces and exact round shapes.

entry_points.name: surface_point
entry_points.summary: Point at (u, v): each control row is reduced at v in homogeneous coordinates, then the column at u.

entry_points.name: revolve_profile
entry_points.summary: Surface of revolution about Y: an (r, y) NURBS profile times the nine-point exact circle.

entry_points.name: sphere_surface
entry_points.summary: Exact sphere: a five-point rational semicircle from the south to the north pole, revolved.

entry_points.name: torus_surface
entry_points.summary: Exact torus: the nine-point circle of the tube cross-section, revolved.

entry_points.name: wave_surface
entry_points.summary: A bicubic free-form patch over [-1.5, 1.5]^2 with a 5 x 5 control net and unit weights.

entry_points.name: tessellate
entry_points.summary: A grid mesh of u_samples x v_samples points evenly spaced in the parameters, normals from central differences in parameter space. ``closed_v`` leaves out the repeated last column of a closed direction.

entry_points.name: build
entry_points.summary: The tessellated demonstration surface the command line writes.

entry_points.name: main
entry_points.summary: Command line: write the tessellated surface (.gltf or .obj) and print a JSON summary.

parameters.name: shape
parameters.meaning: Demonstration surface: exact sphere, exact torus or a free-form wave patch.

parameters.name: u_samples
parameters.meaning: Grid lines across the first parameter.

parameters.name: v_samples
parameters.meaning: Grid lines across the second parameter.

outputs.content: the tessellated surface with POSITION and NORMAL
the same surface as Wavefront OBJ

limits: Uniform parameter sampling, not curvature adaptive. The sphere's poles and the closed seam are repeated grid points, so closed results are watertight after welding. Normals come from central differences in parameter space, with mesh normals at the poles.
technique_references: Surface of revolution from a NURBS profile and the nine-point circle
